First failures were retained privately: shared AX Go returned `429 GoUsageLimitError`; an available official DeepSeek route was then selected only in this isolated Profile through the existing owner. The first official-route trace included an unnecessary own-Bot schedule read; explicit Tob guidance fixed routing, and the fresh successful trace used only scoped schedule CLI. Evidence-driver author-field and panel-visibility corrections were kept separate from product behavior. Outdated drivers were stopped.

Generation 100 is an additive table migration, but it advances the shared operational database generation. Older builds reject this newer generation. A plain Git revert does not downgrade an already upgraded Profile; recovery needs a compatible forward build or a pre-upgrade backup, with later state preserved before restoration. Never delete receipts or lower the generation marker to force a downgrade.

Native continuation diagnostics: the first copied-Profile attempt ended `blocked` before any model step or tool call because its Session cwd still named the original Web home while the Registry derived the copied Desktop home. That attempt remains failed; a fresh Profile was seeded at its final absolute home instead of repairing old history. On the fresh second attempt, both native creation and title change completed through reviewed Shell calls, and the stopped Profile's canonical schedule title and handled Human Source Event confirm the change. The verifier falsely reported a missing update because the bounded 200-character Shell-argument preview omitted the command. The revised driver matches the review's command and exact fresh `parentShellCallId`, retains completed-turn/handled-delivery/reply/canonical checks, and offers read-only `change-read` continuation. An offline replay of that captured truncated call passes the new match and rejects wrong or stale call IDs. This diagnostic is not completion of the remaining native fire/pause/direct/restart acceptance phases.


Native restart revealed a real startup defect after the resumed journey: two earlier planned firings genuinely completed and sent the synthetic marker, but a later missed occurrence was admitted during Desktop startup before the native credentials Service existed. Its canonical Source Event remained retryable, with no Session, observation or side effect. This was not an interrupted model call during shutdown. The original driver only required at least one handled history row, so its PASS was insufficient for startup acceptance. [The visible failure](native-startup-failure-before-fix.png) and [sanitized canonical correlation](native-startup-failure.json) are retained. The candidate fix declares the real credentials Service dependency before core recovery/catch-up; source regression and a new native startup run remain pending at this record. No failure history was deleted or rewritten.


Startup fix source head: `fb6cf4ff011594bcc80bdaa28e4b03136306dc94`. The delayed real native Credential Provider regression reproduced the old race (2 red tests), then passed both cases with the dependency fix: exactly one handled catch-up Source Event, no duplicate on another tick, and available core/bridge with an unconfigured Provider while model execution still refuses safely. Root TypeScript and one build passed. This source proof does not replace the pending native startup rerun. The original 48 management regressions remain bounded to the earlier product head.


Final recovery source head: `5ae3ed1f8dd966a64756bfb93dede338ad668cf1`. The old runtime failed the durable restart regression because neither safe pending nor retryable schedule work woke. The corrected owner path passed 30 checks across three files (including the two credential lifecycle cases, one mixed-state/repeated-restart recovery case, and existing Schedule owner tests); root TypeScript and one build passed. The same eligibility is applied on startup and harvest collection, so a safe item cannot carry uncertain, side-effecting, orphaned, resolved, future-snoozed or paused-Bot work into execution. A recovered schedule clears its prior canonical error only after real handled completion; the captured first failure remains immutable evidence. Disabled stops future occurrences and does not revoke already admitted work. Native startup-arm/prove after this head is still pending.
